R0215.title: Metaverse Social Engineering Attack
R0215.definition: Immersive virtual environments reduce user vigilance, allowing attackers to build trust through virtual identities before launching phishing and fraud attacks.

references.title: Research on metaverse development status and security risks
Defining and Building the Metaverse - The World Economic Forum

R0215.description:
Metaverse social engineering uses immersive spaces, virtual identities, and real-time interaction to build trust. Attackers may impersonate friends, support staff, hosts, or partners to obtain credentials, move virtual assets, or drive users to malicious entry points.

Immersive presence and social pressure can make phishing more persuasive. Platforms need identity indicators, contextual risk prompts, and step-up confirmation for high-risk actions.
R0215.influence: Immersive social engineering can make phishing and fraud more persuasive, leading to credential loss, asset transfer, and user harm.

observables: Newly registered virtual identities build trust with multiple users in a short window and guide asset transfers
Customer-service or partner identities in virtual spaces lure users into clicking external links or leaking credentials
Users show clustered asset loss or credential leakage after immersive interactions
High-risk operations such as transfers and authorizations lack secondary confirmation and are abnormally triggered
Virtual-identity behavior patterns highly match known fraud-ring profiles
